drafted_from: tool:place-sound-effect-cues-into-an-effects-layer row in tools/generate-and-judge-sound-effects/tool-rows.json, its script in tools/generate-and-judge-sound-effects/do-work/ and tools/generate-and-judge-sound-effects/test/test_judge_sound_effects.py (run for real on made-up tones)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Place the cues in /work/sfx/cues.json from palette /work/sfx/a into one effects-only track at /work/sfx/a-layer.wav and tell me its loudness." It runs the placer and reads the layer's LUFS.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it reads CUES.json and the palette's WAV files on this computer and writes one WAV layer.
instructions: 1. Have a palette folder with one <sound>.wav per sound (for example /work/sfx/a/hit.wav and tick.wav).

3. Say "Place my cues". The AI reads the row with tools:list and runs: python3 -I tools/generate-and-judge-sound-effects/do-work/place_cues_into_an_effects_layer.py /work/sfx/a /work/sfx/cues.json /work/sfx/a-layer.wav
4. Read the last line: result.layer and result.lufs. Cues are placed at whole milliseconds with their gain and summed, with no music and no voice.

worked_examples.title: Three cues over 3 seconds make a layer at -13.9 LUFS
worked_examples.ask: Place my sound cues into an effects-only track.
worked_examples.given: From tools/generate-and-judge-sound-effects/test/test_judge_sound_effects.py (test_cues_are_placed_at_whole_milliseconds_with_their_gain_and_summed, run for real): palette a holds hit.wav (0.3 s, 200 Hz, level 0.4, stereo) and tick.wav (0.05 s, 2000 Hz, level 0.4, stereo); cues.json is {"DUR": 3.0, "cues": [[0.5, "hit", 0.0], [1.0005, "tick", -6.0], [2.0, "hit", -3.0]]}. Command: python3 -I tools/generate-and-judge-sound-effects/do-work/place_cues_into_an_effects_layer.py /work/sfx/a /work/sfx/cues.json /work/sfx/a-layer.wav
worked_examples.hands_back: It prints "/work/sfx/a-layer.wav integrated -13.9 LUFS" and the last line {"result": {"layer": "/work/sfx/a-layer.wav", "lufs": -13.9}}. The layer is 3 s, 48000 Hz, 2 channels, silent before 0.5 s, and the 1.0005 s cue starts at 1.000 s.
